Captions in 2026: Free, Paid and the Kenyan Proofreading Problem

5 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

In many regions, CapCut's Auto Captions now carries a Pro badge. Meanwhile, the app you're posting to may caption your video for free. Most creators pay for something they already have.

Captions matter because many people scroll with the sound off: in a matatu, at work, next to a sleeping baby. If they can't follow without sound, they swipe. But how you add captions in 2026 depends on what your CapCut shows you.

OptionCostBest for
CapCut Auto CaptionsFree in some regions/versions; Pro-badged or limited in othersStyled, animated captions you control fully
TikTok's own auto captions (in the posting editor)FreeQuick talking videos posted only to TikTok
CapCut manual Text toolFreeShort videos with a few key lines
Auto captions on YouTubeFreeLong videos; not burned into the picture

If you have CapCut Auto Captions

  1. Tap Text, then Auto captions. Choose the spoken language, and CapCut drops timed captions onto their own track.
  2. Open the caption list view and proofread everything in one scroll instead of tapping each clip.
  3. Style one caption: bold font, white text with a black outline or box. Apply to all.
  4. Drag the captions into the middle third of the screen. The top and bottom get covered by usernames, buttons and the progress bar.
💡 The Kenyan proofreading problem

Auto-transcription tends to struggle with Kenyan names, Swahili and Sheng, and terms like M-Pesa, Till, KSh, Gikomba or Kawangware. A caption reading "Empress Are" instead of "M-Pesa Till" tells a viewer you didn't check, and it confuses search, because TikTok uses the words in and around your video to work out what it's about.

📋 Words to always check in auto captions
Money: M-Pesa, Till, Paybill, KSh / KES, bob, ngiri
Places: [YOUR AREA], [YOUR TOWN], [YOUR MARKET OR ESTATE]
Brand: [YOUR BUSINESS NAME], [YOUR PRODUCT NAMES]
Swahili/Sheng you use often: [e.g. sasa, poa, manze, uko wapi]
Numbers: prices, phone numbers, dates (auto-captions often mis-hear these)
✗ MYTH

Captions are just for deaf viewers and people on mute.

✓ REALITY

They also help search. TikTok's Creator Rewards formula includes a 'search value' metric based on popular search terms, and TikTok matches videos to searches using the words around them. A caption that says your keyword clearly gives the system one more clue about who should see the video.

  • Keep 3–6 words on screen at a time so viewers watch rather than read.
  • If Auto Captions is paywalled for you, add 3–5 manual text lines for the key moments instead of every word.
  • Burned-in captions (in CapCut) survive when you repost to Reels or Shorts; TikTok's own captions don't travel with the file.
✅ Do this today
⚡ Quick check

Auto Captions shows a Pro badge in your CapCut. What's the smartest free move for a TikTok-only talking video?

TikTok's posting editor offers its own auto captions at no cost. For a video that's only going to TikTok, that's often enough. Burned-in CapCut captions matter more when you repost the same file to other apps.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. Auto Captions may be free, limited or Pro depending on your region and version.
  2. TikTok's own captions are a free fallback for TikTok-only posts.
  3. Always proofread Kenyan names, Swahili, Sheng and M-Pesa terms.
  4. Middle third, 3–6 words at a time.
